summary: Add missing test coverage for the shipped teardown harvest + win32 removal fallback per §4/§7; log unreadable friction dirs

edit.description: harvestFriction's readdir catch (~1183-1189, currently one silent catch-all): distinguish absent dir (ENOENT, silent no-op — no friction written this tick) from an unreadable dir, which §4 names alongside 'locked file' as a failure class that must log-and-continue, not swallow silently.

Cover harvestFriction (~1168-1228) e2e via dispatcher.tick(): a fanout worktree's friction file moves into the primary dir tag-prefixed before worktree removal; a per-file move failure logs and the wave still ships; undeclared chain.friction and a relocated state root are no-ops. Prior attempt at this coverage (dangling commit 2135c50, reverted for touching out-of-scope paths) has a directly reusable shape.

Cover removeWorktree (git.ts:90) per §7: a worktree the bare `git worktree remove --force` clears cleanly still succeeds; a path that bare removal fails on is cleared via the prune+bounded-retry fallback; a path surviving even the fallback throws naming the path (Dispatcher aggregates and reports once per wave, not tested here). Note the reverted 2135c50 draft tested a since-abandoned `removeWorktreeWithFallback`-returns-boolean shape — adapt to the shipped throws-on-total-failure API, don't reapply verbatim.

tests.asserts: teardown harvest moves worktree-local friction files into the primary dir tag-prefixed before removal; a per-file harvest failure logs and the wave still ships; undeclared/relocated state root is a no-op.
removeWorktree succeeds via the bare path when clean, succeeds via the prune+retry fallback when the bare call fails, and throws naming the path when even the fallback leaves it behind.

acceptance: tests/Dispatcher.test.ts and tests/git.test.ts assert §4's harvest and §7's removal fallback; TEARDOWN-HARDENING (a94767e) ships with committed coverage instead of none; an unreadable friction dir logs instead of silently no-op'ing.
notes: Same defect shape as FRICTION-GITIGNORE-TESTS/FRICTION-DECLARATION-TESTS: TEARDOWN-HARDENING's own entry named tests[] but a prior attempt with those tests (2135c50) was reverted for touching paths outside files.edit, and the shipped attempt (a94767e) went src-only. This entry lists the test paths explicitly under files.edit.

summary: Write the operator's copy of an afterCommit gate-revert verdict to the friction channel per §5

per.section: 5. Revert note — the operator's copy of the verdict

edit.description: runFanoutEntry's afterCommit gate-revert branch (~962-981): when Chain.friction is declared, write <friction>/<ISO>--<tag>--reverted.md (gate name, message, details, reverted commit subject+body) before git.dropLastCommit discards it, per §5.

tests.asserts: an afterCommit gate revert with Chain.friction declared leaves a note file with the gate's name/message/details and the reverted commit's subject+body; absent when undeclared.

acceptance: An entry-scope afterCommit revert, with Chain.friction declared, leaves a dated --tag--reverted.md note in the primary friction dir carrying the gate verdict and the discarded commit's message; undeclared chains are unaffected.
notes: Only the plan-addressed half of the dev-9175-cim-usage finding (persisting the verdict where plan itself reads it) is explicitly out of scope per §5 — see open-questions.md.

summary: Surface friction counts on status/loop/job-status and switch job extract off the legacy friction.md guess per §6

edit.description: flume status (~630-635) and flume job status (~343-369): append a friction count line when declared and non-empty, per §6.

jobStatus: expose friction count for cli.ts's job-status line. jobExtract (~727-736): when declared, read the friction dir off the job's working tree (fs, not git show — gitignored content was never committed) and print path+content per file, replacing the legacy hardcoded friction.md guess; undeclared keeps today's harvestPaths behavior exactly.
superviseLoop's end-of-run summary: append the same friction count line per §6.

tests.asserts: status and job-status print a friction count line when declared+non-empty, omit it otherwise.
job extract prints the declared friction dir's files (path+content) instead of the legacy friction.md guess; an undeclared chain's extract output is unchanged.

acceptance: status, job status, and loop-end summaries print `friction: N note(s) await routing` when Chain.friction is declared and non-empty; job extract prints the declared dir's files instead of guessing friction.md; undeclared chains are byte-for-byte unchanged.
notes: Friction is gitignored by design (operator ruling, a326c1c) — job extract must read it from the working tree, not git history; the existing harvestPaths loop uses git show and cannot see it.
